boards.title: Your First Weekend at Saint Johns University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A daytime-to-evening first-weekend loop through Saint John’s named campus destinations, with space for art, study, recreation, and the lakeside trail.

cards.entity_name: Saint John's Abbey and University Church
cards.title: Start with the Abbey Church
cards.subtitle: A campus landmark and worship space
cards.notes: Begin by orienting yourself at the church, then use its exterior and plaza as a clear meeting point before walking toward the library.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable starting point for a self-guided campus loop.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint John’s identifies the Abbey & University Church as the central hub of worship for both the university and monastery.
cards.access_notes: Follow posted worship and building-access guidance.

cards.title: Find your academic base at Alcuin
cards.subtitle: Library and Dietrich Reinhart Learning Commons
cards.notes: Walk through Alcuin to locate study rooms, research help, and the Learning Commons so your first class week has a familiar reset point.
cards.short_summary: A practical first stop for study spaces and academic support.
cards.evidence_claim: Alcuin Library includes the Dietrich Reinhart Learning Commons, with study rooms, classrooms, a video studio, editing lab, and coffee shop.
cards.access_notes: Use current library hours and access policies before planning a study session.

cards.title: Step into HMML's exhibitions
cards.subtitle: Lower level of Alcuin Library
cards.notes: From Alcuin’s main entrance, head to the lower level for HMML’s exhibitions and note the route for a future reading-room visit.
cards.short_summary: A museum-and-manuscript stop inside the library complex.
cards.evidence_claim: HMML welcomes visitors to its Reading Room and Exhibitions and is accessed through Saint John’s University Alcuin Library.
cards.access_notes: HMML lists Monday–Friday hours; confirm current exhibition and reading-room availability before visiting.

cards.title: Locate the Saint John's Bible Gallery
cards.subtitle: Alcuin Library partner space
cards.notes: Keep the library visit going by finding the Bible Gallery and checking whether a tour or exhibition program fits your weekend timing.
cards.short_summary: A named gallery stop connected to the university’s manuscript resources.
cards.evidence_claim: The Saint John’s Bible Gallery is listed as a building partner at Alcuin Library, and HMML provides information on its exhibits and public tours.
cards.access_notes: Check HMML’s current information for Bible Gallery exhibits, tours, and class-visit availability.

cards.title: Browse the Art Center galleries
cards.subtitle: Visual-art studios and rotating exhibitions
cards.notes: Make a daylight stop at the Art Center to see which gallery exhibitions are currently installed and to get familiar with the building’s creative spaces.
cards.short_summary: A visual-art stop with named galleries and studios.
cards.evidence_claim: The Saint John’s Art Center has gallery spaces with rotating exhibitions and includes Target, Alice R. Rogers, and Exit galleries.
cards.access_notes: Campus security lists Art Center building access from 6 a.m. to midnight; verify gallery availability separately.

cards.title: Visit the Saint John's Pottery studio
cards.subtitle: Saint Joseph Hall beside the Art Center
cards.notes: Continue west to the pottery studio, look through the gallery, and ask about a guided tour if one is available during your visit.
cards.short_summary: A working campus pottery studio with visitor gallery access.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint John’s Pottery welcomes visitors to its studio gallery, ceramics sales, and guided tours; it is housed in Saint Joseph Hall next to the Art Center.
cards.access_notes: The pottery lists visitor hours on its contact page; confirm tour availability before arriving.

cards.title: Get oriented at Warner Palaestra
cards.subtitle: Campus recreation facility
cards.notes: Use the Palaestra as an active afternoon waypoint: identify the pool, courts, track, and fitness areas, then check current eligibility and hours.
cards.short_summary: A named recreation center with courts, track, pool, and fitness space.
cards.evidence_claim: Warner Palaestra was created as an SJU recreation center and includes an arena, indoor track, fitness room, and Olympic-size pool.
cards.access_notes: Review current athletic-facility hours and eligibility before using recreation spaces.

cards.title: Head to Lake Sagatagan Beach
cards.subtitle: Beachfront trailhead on Lake Sagatagan
cards.notes: Use the beach as the outdoor pivot for the afternoon; check local conditions and posted guidance before swimming or checking out equipment.
cards.short_summary: The lakeside launch point for beach recreation and the Chapel Trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The university’s Lake Sagatagan page identifies a beach and rentals for canoes, kayaks, and paddleboards for campus community members.
cards.access_notes: The beach page publishes seasonal hours and eligibility; check the current page and lifeguard instructions on arrival.

cards.title: Walk the Chapel Trail
cards.subtitle: Lake Sagatagan beachfront to Stella Maris Chapel
cards.notes: Choose the marked three-mile round trip when you have daylight, water, and walking shoes; stay on the route and follow its no-dogs, no-bikes rules.
cards.short_summary: A public lakeshore hike connecting the beachfront with the chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: The Chapel Trail is a three-mile round trip, open to the public, beginning and ending at Lake Sagatagan’s beachfront.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; no dogs or bikes. Plan the hike for daylight and observe posted trail conditions.

cards.title: Finish at Stella Maris Chapel
cards.subtitle: Chapel Trail destination on Chapel Island
cards.notes: Pause at the chapel after the lakeside hike, then return by the same trail; treat the site as a worship and reflection space while visiting.
cards.short_summary: A historic chapel reached on foot along Lake Sagatagan.
cards.evidence_claim: Stella Maris Chapel is reached by a two-mile hike along Lake Sagatagan’s shore and is a destination in the Abbey Arboretum.
cards.access_notes: Use the Chapel Trail’s posted rules and conditions; the chapel is intended as a space for prayer, meditation, worship, or faith celebration.
